# Kafka Compatibility

Kafka compatibility is a collection of specific API, version, and workflow
claims, not a single yes-or-no property. Check the release matrix before choosing
a client or enabling a Kafka feature. This site currently documents `v0.1.3`.

<!-- capability-matrix:start -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/render-capabilities.sh. -->

**Documented release:** `v0.1.3` (`7b0daab0b18166216fbca2c046895f547436902c`)

**Status summary:** 5 verified, 45 experimental,
3 unimplemented, and 4 design targets. The broker
advertises 35 Kafka APIs, but advertising is not verification.

### Experimental System Capabilities

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Object-log-backed produce and fetch</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> The default release test uses the in-memory object store (MemoryBlobStore); the S3 lane self-skips without external configuration. Client ack modes are not passed through to the object-log durability level.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Kafka acks=0, acks=1, and acks=all mapping</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> v0.1.3 hardcodes the strongest sequencing boundary (Ack::Sequenced) for all requests; acks=0 suppresses a response but does not select a distinct backend boundary.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Durable consumer groups and offsets</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> Committed offsets use the shared coordinator store (CoordinatorStore), but wire group membership and generation state use Heimq process memory. The restart smoke retains the same in-memory coordinator and does not prove process-loss durability.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Kafka transactions and exactly-once semantics</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> Coordinator transaction primitives exist, but the Kafka wire path uses Heimq process-local transaction state and is not connected to Fjord&apos;s last stable offset or aborted ranges.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Stateless multi-broker routing</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> Tests share an in-memory coordinator and object store in one process. Membership is a static peer list rather than coordinator-owned monotonic leases. Leader-reassignment split-brain behavior lacks direct release evidence.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Postgres coordinator backend</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> Postgres-gated tests return early when FJORD_PG_URL is unset; the v0.1.3 workspace audit did not exercise an external Postgres service. The running wire group, transaction, and membership paths are not fully backed by the shared coordinator store (CoordinatorStore).</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>S3-compatible durable object storage</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> The Garage test self-skips without FJORD_GARAGE_ENDPOINT and did not exercise external storage in the v0.1.3 workspace audit. Garage range-read compatibility and 100M durable-scale evidence remain open.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Failure, fencing, and history-checker evidence</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> Fault-injected coordinator tests pass, but broker split-brain and Jepsen or equivalent external histories remain open.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Release-mode latency, throughput, and cost evidence</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> The default workspace run omits durable external-store benchmarks and real Kafka or Redpanda comparator lanes.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Helm deployment assets</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> The chart renders and lints, but this audit did not run a release-tagged Kubernetes deployment. The release workflow uploads the packaged chart as a workflow artifact rather than a durable chart repository.</p>
</details>


### Unimplemented System Capabilities

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Local aligned-chunk read cache with deduplicated concurrent reads</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> v0.1.3 passes every fetch directly to the configured object store (BlobStore); no read cache or concurrent-request deduplication exists.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Initial-to-reorganized object-layout compaction</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> v0.1.3 writes a flat initial object layout (L0) and has no background rewrite or atomic switch to the reorganized layout (L1).</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Operational metrics</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> v0.1.3 emits tracing logs but exposes no Fjord metrics endpoint or operational metric instruments.</p>
</details>


### Design Targets Outside the Current Release

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Time and size based topic retention</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> Coordinator truncate primitives exist, but the release backend declares no retention capability.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Kafka compacted topics</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> The design defers cleanup.policy=compact semantics; this is separate from reorganizing the object layout.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>TLS, SASL, ACL, and quota enforcement</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> v0.1.3 does not advertise SASL APIs or expose Fjord TLS, authentication, authorization, ACL, or quota configuration.</p>
</details>

<details class="capability-entry">
<summary><strong>Kafka Connect, MirrorMaker, and ecosystem certification</strong></summary>
<p><strong>Current constraint:</strong> The design defers ecosystem certification and v0.1.3 contains no Fjord release gate for it.</p>
</details>

## Reading the Matrix

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Verified | Passing executable evidence exists for the documented release. |
| Experimental | An implementation exists, but the required release evidence is incomplete. |
| Unimplemented | Active-scope behavior is missing and is mapped to tracked work. |
| Design target | Intended behavior is defined, but it is outside active delivery scope. |

An API advertised by the broker is not automatically **Verified**. Verification
requires the evidence recorded for the documented release. Likewise, success in
one client workflow does not imply support for every version or option of the
underlying APIs.

For evaluation:

1. Match your client workflow to matrix entries, not only API names.
2. Check the documented release and evidence reference.
3. Treat Experimental entries as incomplete.
4. Review [known limitations](limitations.md) for cross-cutting constraints.
